title: Your first workshop
summary: From clay and andesite to the first working Deployer.
text:
# Your first workshop

Start small. A shelter, food supply and a dependable place to keep materials are enough to begin. The first factory grows from ordinary clay and andesite; it does not need a boss kill or a visit to another dimension.

## 1. Make your first alloy

Craft **two Andesite and two Clay Balls into one Andesite Alloy**. Use the alternating 2 × 2 pattern shown in JEI. Logs, planks and slabs retain their normal wood-specific crafting recipes.

Apply Andesite Alloy to a stripped log or stripped wood for an **Andesite Casing**, using Create's normal in-world application.

## 2. Bootstrap an Andesite Machine

The first **Makeshift Mechanism** costs four Andesite Alloy, four wooden slabs and one Iron Ingot. Arrange alloy in the corners, slabs on the edges and iron in the centre.

Surround one Andesite Casing with **eight Makeshift Mechanisms** to craft an **Andesite Machine**. Makeshift is the deliberately expensive manual route to this same machine body. There is no separate Kinetic Machine tier.

Makeshift Mechanisms must be made in your inventory grid or a crafting table. Their automated replacements arrive with the first Deployer.

## 3. Build the first Deployer

Craft the Gold Hand shown in JEI, then combine it with an Andesite Machine. Its registry name is still Brass Hand, even though this pack's bootstrap uses gold.

Power your workstation with Create's early rotational equipment. Use belts or a Depot to carry the workpiece under each Deployer. Check direction and speed before feeding a stack of ingredients.

## 4. Switch to Rotation Mechanisms

A wooden slab receives Andesite Alloy twice and then an Iron Hammer. The assembly takes one pass and yields one Rotation Mechanism; the hammer loses durability. Eight Rotation Mechanisms around a casing now produce the same Andesite Machine more efficiently.

Once a Mixer is available, **one Andesite plus one Clay Ball makes one Alloy**. Automating this ratio is a practical first saving.

## What to do next

- Build a [chute stone generator](../automation/).
- Establish [rubber and Copper production](../progression/chapter-03/).
- Open [Character](../character/) and choose an [origin](../origins/).
- Hover supported items and hold **W** for [Ponder lessons](../ponder/).

Use JEI for the exact installed recipe. The [progression guide](../progression/) follows the current production scripts.

title: The ten chapters
summary: The current route from Manual production to the Creation Core.
text:
# The ten chapters

Create forms the manufacturing backbone. Each chapter adds a useful production capability, then connects it to the next. Adventure and magic supply discoveries and materials without a blanket lock on dimensions or the Wither.

**Chapter numbers run I–X. Internal production tiers run 0–9.** Manual and automated Andesite both construct the same Andesite Machine.

| Chapter | Main component | What opens up |
|---|---|---|
| [01 · Manual](chapter-01/) | Makeshift Mechanism | Clay, Andesite Alloy and the first manually crafted machine body. |
| [02 · Andesite](chapter-02/) | Rotation Mechanism | Affordable repeated machinery and the first automated material loop. |
| [03 · Copper](chapter-03/) | Sealed Mechanism | Tree sap, rubber, fluids and improved logistics. |
| [04 · Brass](chapter-04/) | Precision Mechanism | Heated alloys, precise assembly, controls and Crushing Wheels. |
| [05 · Calculation](chapter-05/) | Calculation Mechanism | Create-built processors and practical ME logistics. |
| [06 · Reinforced](chapter-06/) | Reinforced Mechanism | Steel, electrum, wires and the first electrical engineering projects. |
| [07 · Industrial](chapter-07/) | Industrial Mechanism | IE heavy processing and the 4× ore chain. |
| [08 · Arcane](chapter-08/) | Arcane Mechanism | Source, Mana and magical materials join the production line. |
| [09 · Eclipse](chapter-09/) | Eclipse Mechanism | Chromatic materials, ink recovery and the 5× ore finish. |
| [10 · Creation](chapter-10/) | Creation Core | The final shared project for your entire factory. |


## Mechanisms, bodies and working machines

A mechanism is a production component. A machine body is a crafting ingredient used to construct equipment. Placing a decorative body does not turn it into the corresponding processor.

The early bodies are **Andesite**, **Copper** and **Brass**. **Calculation Machine** leads to AE2 construction. Native **Light Engineering** and **Heavy Engineering Blocks** remain the bodies consumed by their current IE construction recipes; Workshop-style Light/Heavy machine models also exist, but should not be substituted for the native blocks in a recipe.

The **Creation Core** is the final assembly project. The scripts also craft a Creation Machine from eight cores and a Netherite Block; its functional uses are still unassigned.

## Build for repeatable output

Use dedicated lines for Alloy, Rotation, Sealed and Precision Mechanisms before moving on to processors. A late assembly still consumes the earlier mechanisms. Keep buffers of common sheets, tubes, rubber, Redstone and silicon.

Most main mechanism sequences use **one loop and a guaranteed output**. The Creation Core deliberately runs **two passes through nine Deployers**. Read each chapter for fluid amounts and tool wear.

## Exploration stays part of the world

Factory ingredients and local mod mechanics still matter. The Twilight Forest retains its own progression; End Remastered retains its native eye requirements. These are separate from a global pack chapter lock.

No new boss-to-eye table is configured in the current custom loot script. The [adventure guide](../exploration/) explains what is confirmed.

title: A factory that keeps working
summary: Stone generators, buffers, ore yields and durable assembly tools.
text:
# A factory that keeps working

Make reliable inputs before increasing speed. A slow line with a buffer is easier to expand than a fast line that starves every other machine.

## Chute stone generators

These generators use ordinary Water/Lava formation and Create's Mechanical Drill optimization. The **normal Chute goes directly below the generated block**. The **catalyst goes directly below the adjacent Lava source**. The two positions are different.

Keep the Water source separate from the output and use a drop trench for flowing Water where the Ponder shows it. Place the Drill behind the formation cell, facing it. Establish fluids and supports before starting the machine.

| Catalyst under Lava | Generated block |
|---|---|
| Andesite | Andesite |
| Veridium | Veridium |
| Ochrum | Ochrum |
| Asurine | Asurine |
| Scoria | Scoria |
| Diorite | Diorite |
| Crimsite | Crimsite |
| Limestone | Limestone |

Catalysts are retained. A Smart Chute, Hopper or catalyst below the output does not activate the custom rule. Without the matching arrangement, normal formation remains. **Replace the Drill after changing the catalyst** so Create refreshes its cached prediction.

Hover the stone item in a quest task and hold **W** for the in-game construction lesson.

## Ore yields increase with your factory

| Stage | Operation | Yield per original Raw |
|---|---|---:|
| Manual / Andesite | Smelting or Millstone processing | 1× |
| Brass | Crushing Wheels: 1 Raw → 2 Crushed | 2× |
| Industrial | IE Crusher: each Crushed → 2 Dust | 4× |
| Eclipse | Eclipse Lens: 4 Dust → 5 Ingots | 5× |

The shared chain covers **Iron, Copper, Gold, Zinc, Aluminium, Nickel, Lead, Silver and Uranium**. Zinc has a real custom dust. Packed Raw blocks yield 18 Crushed. Refined metal cannot be recycled back into a multiplying stage.

Raw-ore doubling does not add three metal nuggets. Renewable ore-stone recipes can retain their specified nugget bonus. Crushing Wheels receive one 10% Experience Nugget roll, with the exactly-one-paintball recipe excluded. Millstone normalization retains primary-output rolls and removes unrelated byproducts from recipes it can safely decode.

## Keep assemblies aligned

Use adjacent Deployers for successive operations; empty spacing is unnecessary. Put an unpowered or stopped buffer before your line, feed each hand the correct ingredient, and arrange a return route only when the recipe needs repeated passes.

**Reusable** does not always mean **free of wear**. Iron Hammers, Certus Wrenches and Screwdrivers lose durability. Processor dies and the Creation assembly’s Boot Drive are retained without wear.

## Reduce dropped-item traffic

Collect stone directly through Chutes, use storage buffers at handoff points, and upgrade to the supported [Infinity Cells](../storage/) when their material tier is available. Those cells replace repeated stone production inside ME storage; they do not duplicate arbitrary items.

title: AE2 & storage
summary: Processor lines, Calculation construction and tiered Infinity Cells.
text:
# AE2 & storage

Start with a storage layout you can understand: separate incoming materials, processing buffers, finished mechanisms and equipment. Sophisticated Storage and Backpacks provide useful local inventories; AE2 connects those supplies to digital logistics and autocrafting.

## Manufacture processors with Create

The Inscriber and Extended Inscriber are replaced by **Sequenced Assembly**. Each printed-part route applies the corresponding reusable die, then a Mechanical Press finishes the part.

| Starting material | Reusable Deployer tool | Printed result |
|---|---|---|
| Silicon | Silicon Press | Printed Silicon |
| Gold Ingot | Logic Processor Press | Printed Logic Circuit |
| Certus Quartz Crystal | Calculation Processor Press | Printed Calculation Circuit |
| Diamond | Engineering Processor Press | Printed Engineering Circuit |
| Entro Crystal | Concurrent Processor Press | Printed Concurrent Circuit |

For each finished processor, start with its printed circuit, deploy **one Redstone**, deploy **one Printed Silicon**, then Press. One pass gives one processor. Redstone is still consumed.

Copy an AE2 die with an Iron Block, the original die held in a Deployer, and a Press. Initial AE2 dies retain their meteorite acquisition. The Concurrent Press retains its ExtendedAE acquisition.

The Crystal Assembler remains for its other work; its construction uses Mechanical Crafters and the Calculation tier. Molecular Assemblers, the Assembler Matrix and ME autocrafting remain.

## Build the network foundation

Craft a **Calculation Machine** from four Quartz Glass in the corners, four Calculation Mechanisms on the sides, and Certus Dust in the centre. One Machine stonecuts into one ME Controller.

Natural Certus, Entro and Amethyst budding remains enabled. Growth Accelerators and the Crystal Fixer are disabled, while native in-world growth and repair mechanics remain. A [Growth Lens line](../progression/chapter-05/) offers another production route.

## Seventeen Infinity Stone Cells

These use ExtendedAE's actual Infinity Cell inventory and energy behavior. Each provides its named resource inside an ME network.

| Tier | Resources | Storage component | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calculation | Cobblestone, Andesite, Diorite, Granite | 1k | Calculation |
| Reinforced | Veridium, Ochrum, Asurine, Crimsite, Scoria, Scorchia, Limestone | 4k | Reinforced |
| Industrial | Stone, Deepslate, Tuff, Calcite, Basalt, Blackstone | 16k | Industrial |

Each craft uses four samples, two Quartz Glass, an **empty** Cell Housing, the matching component and mechanism. Filled resource cells are not ingredients for higher cells. The native water cell is outside this stone-specific change.

## Connected storage

Pretty Pipes modules use progressively more capable Create routing parts. Sophisticated upgrades retain their data-aware serializers; arbitrary filled backpacks are not substituted as generic crafting ingredients.

**Linked Chest and Pouch** construction consumes a native **Light Engineering Block**. Their wool colours and channel/binding behavior remain native.

title: Immersive engineering
summary: Create handles routine manufacturing; IE keeps its distinctive heavy industry.
text:
# Immersive engineering

Create handles repeatable routine manufacturing. Immersive Engineering contributes heavy processing, electrical infrastructure and mineral extraction. This keeps both systems useful without maintaining parallel factories for the same basic task.

## Where the work moved

| Former IE function | Current direction |
|---|---|
| Metal Press | Create Deployers, Presses and rolling operations |
| Sawmill | Create wood processing |
| Bottling Machine | Spout filling |
| Assembler / Automated Workbench | Crafting and Mechanical Crafters |
| Mixer / Alloy Kiln | Create mixing and alloy processing |
| Fermenter / Squeezer / Refinery | Converted recipes and Create Diesel Generators routes |
| Conveyors and routine pipes/pumps | Create item/fluid logistics |

The replacement system preserves supported native recipes through conversions. It does not make every recipe of every addon interchangeable; use JEI to see the installed result.

**Coke Oven, Blast Furnace, Crusher, Arc Furnace, Excavator/Bucket Wheel, wires and distinctive electrical machinery remain relevant.** Immersive Petroleum is outside the selected setup; Create Diesel Generators is the fuel-production direction.

## Reinforced and Industrial construction

Reinforced Mechanisms introduce Light Engineering. Industrial Mechanisms introduce Heavy Engineering and IE Crusher processing. Their native engineering-block recipes consume four Steel Plates, two Treated Wood Planks, two matching mechanisms and one basic Electronic Component.

Electrum and Copper wire use rolling. Aluminium wire uses one Aluminium Ingot for two wires. Use the appropriate mould or reusable tool only when the installed recipe actually requests it.

## Survey before you excavate

The Excavator extracts IE mineral deposits; it does not create mineable ore blocks. Survey the location and arrange power, output sorting and spoil storage before building the complete multiblock.

The integration adds ten resource deposit definitions and ten rare discoveries when their optional materials are available. Original IE pools gain compatible resources and reduced ordinary recipe failure rates.

| Deposit | Primary pool |
|---|---|
| Ferruginous / Copper / Auriferous / Zinc-bearing strata | 60% matching Create stone, 40% matching ore |
| Certus Quartz Pocket | 60% Certus, 20% Sky Stone, 18% Quartz, 2% Fluix |
| Volcanic Strata | Scoria and Scorchia |
| Magnetic Fault | Neodymium and magnetic cave materials |
| Primordial Fossil Bed | Amber, Bone, cave Limestone and Pewen Sap |
| Ambrosial Strata | Ambrosium, Zanite and Holystone |
| Living Root Seam | Liveroot, Iron Ore, Root Strand and Torchberries |

Pools have biome restrictions. Aether and Twilight deposits use their own biome tags; they are not generic Overworld veins. Recipe percentages apply before IE's separate distance/failure behavior.

New deposit definitions do not reroll existing generated vein data. Server pregeneration and retrogen remain separate choices.

title: Your character
summary: Activity progress, the skill budget, titles and mob levels.
text:
# Your character

The **Character** screen brings together your level, activities, skill tree, titles and origin. Find its inventory button or bind **Open Character** in Controls.

## Grow by playing

The character system tracks **exploration, crafting, fishing, farming, combat, engineering and mining**. Each activity has a milestone requirement and reward; requirements grow as you repeat it.

| Activity | Initial requirement | Initial character XP reward |
|---|---:|---:|
| Exploration | 30 | 1,500 |
| Crafting | 30 | 1,800 |
| Fishing | 20 | 3,000 |
| Farming | 40 | 1,000 |
| Combat | 10 | 2,000 |
| Engineering | 10 | 4,500 |
| Mining | 100 | 800 |

These are the supplied configuration's starting milestones, not rewards for every single action. Crafting and engineering use configured qualifying recipes/objectives. Not every decorative recipe awards engineering progress.

Natural-resource receipts, harvest cooldowns, open-water fishing and spawn-source exclusions limit repeat farming. Team contribution rules exist; merely standing near someone does not establish participation.

**Character XP and vanilla experience are separate.** Origin bonuses to fishing or trading XP refer to vanilla orbs; Millwright improves engineering character XP. Unidentified Loot payments use vanilla XP points.

## Level and skill budget

The current tree has **588 one-point nodes** and a **175-point spending limit**, with the supplied description targeting 175 earned points by character level 100. Skills persist through death.

Character growth uses configured progression ceilings. The current ceiling array is **10, 30, 50, 70, 80, 94, 100**, with team unlock sharing enabled. This seven-step character configuration is separate from the ten production chapters; a final quest-to-unlock reward map is still being rebuilt.

Read the [skill guide](../skills/) for the actual configured paths and node effects.

## Origins are a separate choice

The first Character visit opens the origin chooser. Preview one of **20 backgrounds**, inspect its two perks, then confirm. An unconfirmed preview can be closed without choosing.

An origin is stored with the character and is independent of equipped titles or skill respecs. Existing confirmed origins retain their saved revision. [Compare all backgrounds](../origins/).

## Mob levels

The supplied progression config enables mob scaling with a **±4 level variance**. It configures **0.03 health scaling per level** and **0.0125 damage scaling per level**. Excluded spawn sources and boss-specific behavior still matter.

Level badges help communicate the encounter's relative level. They are not a promise that two different species or bosses at the same level have identical health, attacks or difficulty.

title: The current skill tree
summary: 588 connected choices with exact, searchable node effects.
text:
# The current skill tree

Spend points on the effects you use. The current Pufferfish configuration contains **588 nodes**, each costing **one point**, with a total spending limit of **175**. The category has no exclusive-root setting and does not erase skills on death.

## Six configured paths

The imported tree retains six internal path families, each containing 98 nodes. Their IDs are compatibility references, not six mandatory character classes.

| Path family | Entry node caption |
|---|---|
| Alchemist | Potion Longevity |
| Blacksmith | Tempered Craft |
| Cook | Restorative Cuisine |
| Enchanter | Arcane Study |
| Hunter | Prospector's Fortune |
| Miner | Miner |

The live node descriptions have been modernized beyond some historical internal names. Follow the connections and read the effect, rather than assuming an ID implies an old class or profession rule.

## What nodes can change

The configuration includes direct attribute bonuses and scripted passives. Examples include potion duration, resource handling, mining/building utility, recovery and optional magic attributes.

Iron's Spells and Ars bonuses apply through their installed integrations. A description mentioning an optional mod does not make that mod a new hard dependency. Scripted passives can have conditions or caps; their complete node description is shown in the reference.

## Plan with the current data

[Browse every configured node](nodes/) to search by title, internal ID, path or effect. It is a read-only reference to the supplied configuration. It does not spend points or alter your character.

The old web class planner and its six-class/eighteen-subclass restrictions are retired from the current wiki. Skill connections, point availability and server configuration govern the in-game tree.

## Keep your systems distinct

Skill points develop your tree. Activity XP develops your character. An origin adds its own two perks. Titles provide a separate display/passive selection. Owning a title does not automatically apply every title's bonuses at once.

title: Choose your origin
summary: Twenty backgrounds, two perks each, and the rules that matter.
text:
# Choose your origin

Your background gives a small, useful advantage without deciding your equipment or factory path. Open Character, preview a card, and confirm the combination you like. The chooser has three pages and twenty original icons.

| Origin | Perk one | Perk two |
|---|---|---|
| Deepdelver | +10% ore mining speed. | 5% chance for an extra raw ore from natural deposits. |
| Woodcutter | +15% log chopping speed. | 5% chance for an extra natural log. |
| Homesteader | +10% mature crop yield when harvested by hand. | 10% less hunger from exhaustion. |
| Stablehand | 10% shorter animal breeding cooldowns. | +15% movement speed for living mounts you control. |
| Riverfolk | 10% shorter fishing wait. | +15% vanilla fishing XP. |
| Huntsman | +5% bow and crossbow damage. | +10% meat and leather drops from your kills. |
| Forgehand | 10% of anvil repair XP refunded; normal requirements apply. | 10% less weapon durability loss. |
| Stonemason | +15% stone breaking speed. | +0.5 block reach while holding a building block. |
| Millwright | +10% engineering activity XP. | +1 block interaction reach while holding a wrench. |
| Librarian | 10% of enchanting XP refunded; normal requirements apply. | +15% XP recovered through grindstone disenchanting. |
| Apothecary | +15% duration for beneficial potions you drink. | +10% healing from instant health potions you drink. |
| Hedge Herbalist | +10% natural health regeneration. | 10% chance for an extra gathered flower or mushroom. |
| Caravan Trader | 10% lower villager buying prices, rounded down. | +15% vanilla trading XP. |
| Wayfarer | +5% movement speed. | 20% less fall damage. |
| Deckhand | +15% swimming speed. | +5 seconds of underwater breathing time. |
| Town Watch | +1 armour point. | +10% knockback resistance. |
| Street Urchin | +15% sneaking speed. | 10% shorter hostile detection range while sneaking. |
| Gravekeeper | 10% less damage from undead attackers. | +15% vanilla XP from undead kills. |
| Temple Acolyte | +2 maximum health (one heart). | 10% shorter harmful potion effects. |
| Hedge Mage | +5% maximum mana. | +5% mana regeneration. Requires Iron's Spells mana attributes. |


## Understand the perk's scope

- **Deepdelver and Woodcutter:** natural deposits/logs only; suitable tools apply. A bonus is one extra item, not a copied Fortune stack.
- **Homesteader:** mature crop breaks by hand. Other mods' right-click harvesting and machine harvesting are outside this hook.
- **Stablehand:** the speed bonus applies to a living mount you control. Boats use another movement system.
- **Forgehand and Librarian:** refunds use XP points actually spent, preserving normal requirements. Repair refunds require an actual repair; a rename is not enough.
- **Apothecary:** drinking potions, rather than splash or lingering effects.
- **Stonemason and Millwright:** block interaction reach, not attack reach. Hold the appropriate building block or supported wrench.
- **Street Urchin:** reduces sneaking detection range; it does not clear an existing target.
- **Hedge Mage:** requires Iron's maximum-mana and regeneration attributes. Unified mana is handled by the existing integration; no duplicate Ars bonus is added.

Fractional rewards carry forward where the implementation supports them. Stable modifier IDs prevent bonuses stacking through repeated refreshes. Maximum-health bonuses do not immediately heal you.

## Existing characters

Previously confirmed choices retain their saved origin and perk revision. This includes the former Librarian's different refund values. Choosing the new Librarian on a new character uses the values above.

## Changing a choice

Origin administration requires permission level 2 and an online target. It changes the origin, without clearing skills, titles, equipment or character progress.

~~~text
/tnkprogress origin get PlayerName
/tnkprogress origin set PlayerName tnk:deepdelver
/tnkprogress origin reset PlayerName
~~~

After a reset, close and reopen Character. Origin selection is independent of cosmetic and passive titles.

title: The Beta 1.0 questbook
summary: The new groups, populated production chapters and remaining questbook work.
text:
# The Beta 1.0 questbook

Use the book to find your next project, learn a system and track your progress. Beta 1.0 includes the rebuilt chapter layout and the first populated production chapters, alongside inherited quest material.

**The book remains in progress.** The target is at least **1,500 useful quests**. The archive's raw record count includes legacy chapters and unfinished pages, so it does not measure completion of the new campaign.

## The new groups

| Group | What belongs here |
|---|---|
| Town Square | Tutorial, progression overview, Market and Bulletin Board |
| Forging Ahead | The ten main production chapters |
| Crafts & Curiosities | Aeronautics, magic, fishing, nuclear engineering, enchanting and Let's Do paths |
| Realms & Relics | Exploration, Bosses, Useful Items and The Eyes |
| Seasonal Tales | The First Winter seasonal page |

Some of these pages are placeholders while their objectives and rewards are authored. Older Town Square, Mechanical, Adventure and Magical groups also remain in the exported book.

## Main production chapters

[Manual → Andesite → Copper → Brass → Calculation → Reinforced → Industrial → Arcane → Eclipse → Creation](../progression/)

The new pages use player-facing titles such as Getting Started, Rotations & Andesite, Valves & Fluids, Precision Machinery and Light Engineering. These correspond to the production route documented here.

| Chapter | Exported quest records |
|---|---:|
| I · Getting Started | 10 |
| II · Rotations & Andesite | 17 |
| III · Valves & Fluids | 15 |
| IV · Precision Machinery | 26 |
| V · Logic & Energistics | 23 |
| VI · Light Engineering | 26 |
| VII · Heavy Machines | 26 |
| VIII · Magic & Mana | Page in place; objectives pending |
| IX · Radiant & Shadow | Page in place; objectives pending |
| X · The Final Chapter | Page in place; objectives pending |

AE2, Immersive Engineering and Apotheosis belong within the main progression. The recipes for the later chapters are documented even where their quest pages are unfinished.

## Town Square and specialist paths

The Market and Bulletin Board provide the shopping and job-board direction. Their new pages and final reward assignments are still being built.

Specialist pages cover Aeronautics, Witchery, Starcatcher, Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks, Ars Nouveau, Create Nuclear, Enchantment Industry and Let's Do. Exploration brings together Alex's Caves, Twilight Forest, Aether and Deeper and Darker; Bosses and The Eyes track encounter and End Remastered goals.

The First Winter page establishes a Seasonal Tales branch. Its presence does not mean the seasonal questline is complete.

## Ponder from a quest

Hover a supported item in a task and hold **W**. The [97-lesson reference](../ponder/) includes stone generation, processors, mechanisms, industrial multiblocks and Workshop features. The beta includes custom quest icons and artwork with its KubeJS resources.

## Reading inherited chapters

The ZIP contains **42 chapter files and 1,036 records** in total. Some older entries still reference Malum, space progression and the previous eleven-chapter route. Use the [Beta 1.0 mod inventory](../mods/) to check what is installed and the [ten-chapter guide](../progression/) for the current manufacturing route.

title: Unidentified Loot
summary: Identify equipment, compare rarity, discover pools and salvage unwanted finds.
text:
# Unidentified Loot

Bring equipment discoveries back from your expeditions, identify what you find, and decide what deserves a place in your loadout. The custom loot system connects modded equipment with Apotheosis affixes, discovery and salvaging.

## Rarity and tier are different

Tier identifies the equipment/progression band. Rarity controls the quality of its roll. A brighter rarity does not make every lower-tier weapon stronger than every higher-tier one.

| Rarity | Colour |
|---|---|
| Common | White |
| Uncommon | Green |
| Rare | Pink |
| Epic | Purple |
| Legendary | Light blue |
| Mythic | Orange |

The supplied config defines separate ordinary and boss weights, tier affix bands and progression rarity caps. These are weighted rolls, not percentages printed directly from a weight.

## Identify and discover

Use the identifier interfaces and the Create **Mechanical Identifier** where available in the installed mod. The collection and pool previews help you inspect what you have discovered; unexplored rewards can remain silhouettes.

Identification payments use **vanilla XP points**. They are separate from Character activity XP. Check the displayed cost before confirming a batch.

## Boss rewards

The supplied boss-reward config contains **48 pool definitions**. They include encounters from Cataclysm, Iron's Spells, Mowzie's, Twilight Forest, Aether and other equipment-bearing bosses where their items are available.

A configured definition is not proof that a particular encounter spawned in your world. Pools depend on installed IDs, enabled entries and normal loot events. Signature affixes can apply themed effects with configured cooldowns.

## Salvaging

Unwanted discoveries can be salvaged. The supplied feature config enables discovery collection, previews, rarity reveals and salvaging. Salvage values rise with rarity, while XP costs and a maximum refund fraction limit recycling.

The configured rarity credits are **1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20**, with the refund fraction capped at **0.4**. These values belong to the supplied loot configuration; the interface remains the authority for a particular item and mod build.

## Explore beyond the Overworld

Dimension routing covers Aether, Twilight, Nether and End equipment families. Global equipment can coexist with local pools. The selected ports and addons decide which exact pieces are registered.

These rules describe the loot mod and configuration shipped together in Beta 1.0. Use the [current pack reference](../status/) when checking an installation.

title: Magic that meets the workshop
summary: Ars, Iron’s Spells, unified mana and automated scroll production.
text:
# Magic that meets the workshop

Ars Nouveau supplies spell design, Source and magical automation. Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks supplies combat schools, scrolls, spellbooks and equipment. Their integrations let both systems contribute to the factory.

## Ars Nouveau

Develop spell components through Ars' own systems. Source Gems, Sourceberries and compatible focuses connect to Arcane production. Existing Source costs and glyph requirements remain on focus recipes; optional exploration ingredients add alternatives.

Ars Creo and Create Wizardry connect mechanical and magical work. A Mana Siphon exists, but the current Mana bootstrap does not require one: **Arcane Essence plus Water** makes Mana through the defined Mixer route.

## Iron's Spells and Resonant Arcana

Choose equipment and schools for the way you fight. The native Scroll Forge and research acquisition remain relevant.

**Resonant Arcana** is the custom spell addon. Its individual spell roster and balance change with the installed build. The wiki does not turn older proposed spells or hotfix test logs into a fixed current spell-count claim.

Ars 'n Spells provides the selected unified-mana integration. Origins and skill bonuses should apply once through their own supported attributes.

## Build a two-Deployer scroll line

The script discovers enabled, Forge-craftable spells and valid native ink outcomes, including eligible addon spells in supported schools.

1. Put **Paper** under the first Deployer and supply a valid **school focus**.
2. Install an allow-list **Create Filter** containing the desired Unfinished School Scroll **and that held focus**. Enable **Respect Data**.
3. Feed the unfinished scroll to the second Deployer and supply the matching **Ink**.
4. Its Filter must contain **one exact completed spell/level scroll and that Ink**, also with Respect Data.

Each completed scroll consumes one Paper, one focus and one Ink. Filters remain reusable. Including the held ingredient allows the Deployer to restock its hand.

No filter, the wrong school/ink, missing component data or multiple selectable outputs stop processing rather than choosing an arbitrary spell. A direct scroll ghost is not a substitute for the configured list Filter.

Research-required and noncraftable spells retain their native acquisition. Ink cannot be filtered into a stronger outcome than its native rarity permits.

Use the exact spell and level shown in the installed JEI recipe when setting each filter.

## Witchery and other magical paths

Just Another Witchery Remake is included in Beta 1.0 with its own ritual and discovery path, alongside the Ars and Iron's Spells integrations.

## Alchemical Lasers

The five lenses are **Growth, Convergence, Splitting, Power and Eclipse**. Their roles include crystal growth, material conversion and late ore processing. Follow the lens and minimum speed in each recipe.

Beta 1.0 includes Alchemical Lasers with all five lenses. The **Growth Lens** is used for the Calculation chapter's Certus route. Lenses are reusable tooling; recipe input counts still apply.

title: Explore, fight, return
summary: Dimensions, dungeons, combat and the discoveries your workshop can use.
text:
# Explore, fight, return

Build a useful home, then take a reason to leave it. Dungeons, caves, dimensions and bosses bring back equipment, building palettes and ingredients with practical uses.

## The Beta 1.0 world

**Wildshape** supplies the terrain foundation, alongside Regions Unexplored, Biomes O' Plenty and Nature's Spirit. Streams Reflowing adds flowing rivers, with **Flow Control** supplying tools for working with them.

Autumnity, WilderNature, Alex's Mobs, Hybrid Aquatic and Modern Apple Cows contribute environments and wildlife. Alex's Caves adds its distinctive underground regions. ShineaL's Prehistoric Expansion and Realm RPG: Treasure Balloons are not part of Beta 1.0.

Terrain settings affect newly generated chunks. Changing a preset does not reshape a town or rewrite chunks that already exist.

## Choose an expedition

| Destination | What to look for |
|---|---|
| Alex's Caves | Distinct underground regions, themed resources and encounters |
| Aether / Deep Aether | Sky exploration, equipment, Aether villages and local resources |
| Twilight Forest | Its native boss progression, landmarks and materials |
| Deeper and Darker | The Otherside and its discoveries |
| Nether | BetterNether, Amplified Nether and Jaden's Nether Expansion |
| End / BetterEnd | Native eye access, exploration and advanced building materials |

The pack keeps dimension access outside blanket workshop stage locks. Native portal costs, End Remastered and Twilight's own rules still apply.

## Dungeons and encounters

**Archaion**, **Legendary Monsters** and **Bosses'Rise** join Cataclysm and Mowzie's Mobs. Ancient Remnants adds monolith discoveries. Integrated Cataclysm, Integrated Mowzie's Mobs and Integrated Seven Seas expand the encounter and structure selection.

**Epic Structures: Dungeons, Jungle Temples and Witch Huts** take over those three structure roles. YUNG's Desert Temples, Mineshafts, Nether Fortresses, Ocean Monuments and End Island remain in the beta, alongside Integrated Dungeons and Structures, Integrated Dungeons Arise, Integrated Stronghold and Integrated Villages.

Lootr supports per-player container loot where compatible. **Unidentified Loot** connects equipment discoveries to identification, rarity, collection and salvage. **Death Keeper** supplies the beta's gravestone system.

## Combat and camera

Epic Fight and Weapons of Miracles provide action combat and weapon movesets. Punchy! and Punchy! Moves add animation systems, with **Combat Punchy** handling automatic handoffs between Epic Fight and Punchy behavior. The beta also includes the dedicated Punchy / Iron's Spells first-person compatibility addon.

Shoulder Surfing Reloaded, Do a Barrel Roll and Reach Behind provide additional camera and perspective options. Check their controls alongside combat keybinds before changing several settings at once.

## Materials worth bringing home

Alex's Caves resources have routes into magnets, AE2 parts, glue, fertilizer, Arcane Essence and Glow Ink. Aether and Twilight materials can also appear in their own Excavator deposit pools.

These alternate uses complement ordinary discovery. They do not force a boss catalyst into every machine.

## The Eyes and boss rematches

End Remastered retains its native eye acquisition. The beta's custom boss/chest mapping script has no additional assignments.

**Universal Boss Respawner** is included and enabled. Supported encounters can use its boss-rematch cages; follow the displayed revival item and requirements. Boss support follows the installed mod's rules. Quest-token costs and timers remain part of the questbook work.

title: Towns & Kingdoms Workshop
summary: Projectors, construction tools, cages, mirrors and the Trading Hub.
text: # Towns & Kingdoms Workshop Workshop contains the pack's custom utility features. It gives your settlement tools for displaying goals, building, handling selected entities and connecting player destinations. ## Quest Projector Place the Projector and right-click to configure its display. Supported modes include **quests with tasks, images and formatted text**. Saved display settings travel with the configured item. Use it for a workshop objective board, a town sign or a visible shared project. Quest displays read the supported quest integration; an image or text projection does not create a new reward or complete a task. ## Construction tools The supplied JAR includes **Measuring Pencil**, **Builder's Satchel** and **Builder's Brush**. Their in-game controls and tooltips describe the selected operation. They are practical building utilities, rather than substitute machine frames. **Magic Mirror**, **Chorus Mirror** and **Mob Cage** are also present. Dimension, destination and containment restrictions can apply. Boss protection remains relevant; the pack blocks boss jar capture, including the Dragon and Wither. ## Spawner Cage Right-click a spawner to capture it, then right-click a block to place the captured spawner. The Cage is **consumed after placement**. It is a single-use relocation tool, not a reusable spawner farm multiplier. Spawner tooltips expose useful settings such as spawn count, delay range, activation range, spawn range and nearby mob limit. The reward/acquisition route is a separate pack decision; no free recipe is invented here. ## Trading Hub [Open the Trading Hub guide](../trading-hub/) for placement, listing, browsing and teleportation. It uses Waystones/Balm and retains the stable item ID tnkcore:trade_sharestone. ## Ponder compatibility Workshop 0.11.10 includes the optional client integrations for IE multiblock rendering in Ponder and Enchantment Industry bulk-salvaging with Apotheosis materials. The separate older Ponder-render helper is superseded by that build. Match Workshop on clients and the server; keep the full corresponding Ponder resources. ## Discord presence Workshop includes configurable Rich Presence for supported activities, locations and menus. Availability depends on its configuration and a supported desktop Discord session. Presence is a cosmetic integration, not a gameplay requirement.

title: Trading Hub
summary: A directory for player shops and useful destinations.
text: # Trading Hub Give players a place to list a shop, browse the directory and travel to another destination. The floating globe is a block renderer; it does not use a ticking statue entity. ## Obtain and place The current Workshop build **does not give a Hub automatically on login** and removes the old free claim commands. The intended distribution is a configured quest item reward. The stable reward item is tnkcore:trade_sharestone, visibly named **Trading Hub**. The final starter/repeat-purchase reward assignment belongs to the questbook configuration. Place both halves with the normal block item. Placement opens the setup editor. Give the destination a name, description and icon, then save. ## Browse and manage The home screen links to the public shop directory and your personal listings. Search narrows the directory, sorting changes name/owner order, and arrows move through pages. Your owned destinations open their editor. Ownership and block identity are checked by the server; editing a listing does not transfer ownership of another player's block. The supplied icon picker has **130 icons**. Servers can restrict the allowed selection. ## Teleport Open a destination and use **Teleport**. The Hub uses Waystones-backed travel with landing checks and a default five-second cooldown. It is not the same as a paid player-to-player trade transaction. The directory helps players reach a shop; the actual item/currency exchange belongs to the shop system they build. Full multiplayer shop transactions and claims integration still need testing in the final combined pack. ## Keep the listing intact Use the editor or remove the owning block normally. Do not move a Hub on a contraption: moving-base placement is not supported in this beta. Server settings in tnkcore-market-server.toml control text limits, teleport cooldown and icons. Defaults are 40 characters for names and 240 for descriptions. Existing directory data persists in the world's saved data.

title: A home worth returning to
summary: Food variety, decorative materials and practical farming integrations.
text:
# A home worth returning to

The factory supports a comfortable base. Build a kitchen, keep gardens close to storage, and turn exploration's palettes into places you enjoy using.

## Grow variety

Farmer's Delight and Croptopia are part of the selected farming family, alongside Veggies Delight, Corn Delight, fruit/food addons and the Let's Do collection. Use their installed recipe links and cutting-board processing rather than assuming ingredients with similar names are interchangeable.

Spice of Life: Carrot Edition rewards trying different foods. Beta 1.0 sets milestones at **5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 unique foods**, and keeps the recorded food list after death.

The pack disables the confirmed reusable foods **Everlasting Beef, Eternal Steak and conditional Infinity Ham**. Normal meals, Farmer's Delight ham and smoked ham remain ordinary food options.

## Connect the kitchen

Create farms, collection and processing can feed storage and food production. Slice & Dice and compatible integrations connect selected recipes. Preserve a small manual supply while automating crops with longer growth or unusual harvest behavior.

Origins and activities distinguish hand harvesting from machine production. A farm can be useful without every machine-harvested crop earning a player's hand-harvest bonus.

## Materials from the environment

Biomes O' Plenty and Regions Unexplored fibers have hand, Cutting Board and Saw alternatives where configured. Moss can become string and reeds can become paper. These are practical local-material uses, without making every household craft cost a mechanism.

Building automation includes selected BetterEnd, Quark and other materials. Chipped-style workstations, Lili's Pottery and decorative palettes keep their own roles. **Copycats+, Diagonal Fences, Etched and Torchmaster** are included; **Construction Sticks** joins Workshop's building tools.

## Build a town your way

Use shared storage, public workshops, farms, roads and a [Trading Hub](../trading-hub/). Town building in Beta 1.0 centres on player-built settlements; MineColonies is part of the preserved TK2 setup.

title: Titles & rewards
summary: Separate your visible badge from the passive benefit you equip.
text: # Titles & rewards Titles mark achievements, skills, roles and participation. The character interface keeps the **cosmetic display** separate from the **passive title selection**. ## Equip a benefit deliberately Owning several titles does not apply every perk simultaneously. Read the selected passive's descriptions and choose the combination that helps your current project. The supplied perk config uses a **30-second swap cooldown**. Its definitions include chapter-style titles, skill titles, profession/mastery rewards and encounter achievements. Some achievement descriptions still use historical chapter terminology; the final quest reward map is being rebuilt. ## Founder The title ID tnk:beta_tester displays **Founder** with amethyst artwork. It can be selected as a cosmetic title independently of the equipped passive. **Beta 1.0 includes Founder passive bonuses:** First Footsteps adds **3% base movement speed** and Founding Hands adds **5% base block-breaking speed**. These belong to the selected passive; owning the title alone does not stack its bonuses with every other title. ## Reward integration FTB Quests can call the supported title commands from configured rewards. The correct ID must already exist in the installed title catalogue. The wiki does not assign guessed completion triggers to current chapters. Beta 1.0 includes **58 configured titles**. Unlock requirements and quest rewards should use the catalogue shipped with this pack. [Browse the configured title reference](reference/) for IDs and passive descriptions. Origin selection and skill-tree spending are independent systems.

title: Find recipes faster
summary: The exact nineteen tag searches, information pages and Ponder controls.
text: # Find recipes faster JEI is the current lookup for the installed recipe set. The wiki explains the production route; the game resolves enabled mods, tags, conditions and dynamic spell recipes. ## Nineteen useful searches These are ordinary item-tag searches, not new JEI tabs. Type the exact query, including **#**. | Group | Query | Use | |---|---|---| | Progression components | #tnk_progression | Mechanisms, machine frames and key components in the main production chain. | | Machine frames | #tnk_frames | The existing tier machine blocks used to construct processing equipment. | | Processing equipment | #tnk_processing | Create production machines and the retained IE, laser and magic processing stations. | | Automation and logistics | #tnk_logistics | Transport, filters, fluid handling and redstone control. | | Storage | #tnk_storage | Practical inventories, tanks, AE2 storage and the pack infinity cells. | | Factory materials | #tnk_materials | Canonical metals, dusts, sheets and useful production intermediates. | | Magic and enchanting | #tnk_magic | Spell scrolls, lenses, casting equipment and magic workstations. | | Combat equipment | #tnk_combat | Representative melee, ranged and defensive equipment; no decorative variants. | | Bosses and exploration | #tnk_exploration | Boss summoning items, portal eyes, navigation and travel utilities. | | Tools and gadgets | #tnk_tools | Reusable tools for building, engineering and practical base tasks. | | Andesite tier | #tnk_tier_andesite | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Andesite tier. | | Copper tier | #tnk_tier_copper | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Copper tier. | | Brass tier | #tnk_tier_brass | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Brass tier. | | Calculation tier | #tnk_tier_calculation | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Calculation tier. | | Reinforced tier | #tnk_tier_reinforced | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Reinforced tier. | | Industrial tier | #tnk_tier_industrial | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Industrial tier. | | Arcane tier | #tnk_tier_arcane | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Arcane tier. | | Eclipse tier | #tnk_tier_eclipse | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Eclipse tier. | | Creation tier | #tnk_tier_creation | Selected construction recipes and components assigned to the Creation tier. | Groups can overlap. Optional missing items are skipped. These organizational tags are not recipe ingredients and do not unlock progression. ## Read the information Information pages explain processor dies, ore yields, rubber heating, scroll filters, paintballs, Mana, Creation items and other non-obvious behavior. The Wrench and Compass also carry the search-query reference. Short tooltips identify reusable presses and important tool/fluid requirements. An ingredient's internal ID can retain an older name while its visible name has changed. ## Ponder Hover a supported item and hold **W**, or your rebound Ponder key. You can do this directly over an item task in the questbook. The pack provides **97 authored lessons** in the current collection, alongside native lessons supplied by compatible mods. [Search the lesson index](../ponder/). ## When an item is hidden Some entries are compatibility remnants or developer-only items; others are fully disabled for the pack. Hidden-only entries and disabled gameplay are different. [The balance guide](../balance/) explains the selected removals.

title: Balance & removed shortcuts
summary: What is deliberately restricted, and which native systems remain.
text:
# Balance & removed shortcuts

The current pack changes individual crafting/acquisition routes and selected items. It does not impose an automatic chapter lock on every dimension.

## Factory direction

Create replaces routine IE manufacturing and AE2 Inscriber processing. IE's distinctive heavy machines and AE2's storage/autocrafting remain useful.

Growth Accelerators, Crystal Fixer and the ExtendedAE Circuit Cutter are disabled. Natural budding and in-world crystal mechanics remain available.

## Selected acquisition restrictions

The shared catalogue disables Ender Leads, selected mob-capture upgrades, the Spatial Anchor, IE Chunk Loader, the craftable Alex's Caves Nuclear Bomb, selected novelty/flight items and duplicate Rubberworks rubber materials.

Primed Alex's Caves nuclear bomb entities are also blocked by the custom hook. Toxic Caves, the Nuclear Furnace and other nuclear systems remain.

Capturing enchantment is removed from the configured acquisition tags and denied to the printer. Bosses, including the Wither and Dragon, are protected from Ars jar capture.

## Spawners and flight

The spawner runes that ignore conditions, ignore players or remove AI are blocked by the cleanup rules. The ordinary spawner system and single-use Workshop Spawner Cage are separate features.

The selected Apotheosis flying potion route/effect is disabled. The **Angel Ring** is the beta's crafted flight item, with an **11 × 7 Mechanical Crafter** wing recipe at the Arcane tier.

Its forty consumed ingredients include feathers, Gold Blocks, Legendary Ink, Arcane materials, Ignitium, Air Essence, Nether Stars, Wind Charges, a Diamond Ring, Cloud in a Bottle and Golden Amber. Native Ring flight behavior is not rewritten by the recipe.

## Food and recycling

The three confirmed infinite-food items are disabled conditionally when registered. Ordinary meals remain.

The nine-metal ore chain blocks finished metal from returning to its multiplying Dust/Crushed stages. Native Netherite Scrap yields are not increased.

## Visibility is not deletion

Legacy decorative/custom entries and creative-only items can be hidden without being unregistered. Existing worlds may retain stacks and placed blocks. The exact shared catalogue is included in the [source reference](../status/).

Configuration and beta testing can still change the final release. This guide records the inspected package's selected rules rather than claiming every unrelated mod interaction has been tested.

title: Play together
summary: Official regions, shared worlds and keeping client/server files matched.
text:
# Play together

Towns & Kingdoms has an official **EU and US server direction**, with community events and shared projects. Use the pack's current server list and [Discord](https://discord.gg/CRYk3uDPVt) for availability, beta windows, event announcements and joining details.

## Build a shared settlement

Give projects a visible home: a farm supplying the kitchen, a public processor line, a warehouse, roads and shops. A Quest Projector can display goals, while a Trading Hub directory helps players find useful destinations.

FTB Teams and Chunks support group organization and land claims. Progression's team settings govern supported unlock sharing; they do not make every personal choice shared. Origins, equipped titles and skill spending remain character choices.

## Match the installation

Beta 1.0 uses **Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.262 and Java 21**. Use the complete Beta 1.0 files for both the client and the relevant server-side installation.

Keep the same approved custom-mod JARs, KubeJS startup/server/client scripts, required root JSON files, quest files and resources on the relevant sides. A full restart is needed after item registration, protocol or startup changes. Recipe-only edits can be reloaded once the matching installation is in place.

Do not install a TNK2 download expecting it to launch TNK3. The shared CurseForge project's latest public client is still **TK2 3.05 for Forge 1.20.1**.

## Pregeneration and travel

A Minecraft world border's configured size is its diameter. RTP limits are distances from the configured centre. Compare both with the actual pregenerated area before enabling travel.

The supplied FTB Essentials config uses a **25,000 maximum RTP distance**, a **500 minimum** and **600-second cooldown**, with the End excluded. These are source-config values, not a live verification of either official server.

Changing generation presets or Excavator definitions does not rewrite already generated chunks and vein data. Plan those updates before generating a new official world.

## Report a problem

Include the pack snapshot/build, whether it happened in singleplayer or multiplayer, the steps involved and the relevant log/crash report. [Use GitHub issues](https://github.com/Mikaaah/TownsAndKingdoms/issues) or the community's designated support channel.

title: Beta 1.0 files & sources
summary: The authoritative Beta 1.0 archive, complete inventory, source hashes and questbook progress.
text: # Beta 1.0: files and sources **Towns & Kingdoms 3 — Beyond the Forge · Beta 1.0 · 8 November 2026** The uploaded **Beta 1.0 ZIP is the authoritative baseline** for the current mod selection, configs, KubeJS, quests and pack resources. The wiki follows this archive. Earlier exports, separate test installations and proposed additions do not extend its modlist. ## Pack version | Setting | Beta 1.0 | |---|---| | Minecraft | 1.21.1 | | Loader | NeoForge 21.1.262 | | Java | 21 | | CurseForge manifest projects | 315 | | Directly bundled custom mods | 3 | | Bundled mods | TnK Workshop, Unidentified Loot and Wildshape | TnK Progression, Resonant Arcana, Alchemical Lasers, Flow Control and Combat Punchy are included through the manifest. The three bundled mods are additional entries; they are not missing dependencies to fetch from an older export. Libraries are included in the project count, which is different from a runtime count of loaded mod IDs. ## Included systems | Reference | Count | |---|---:| | Production chapters | 10 | | Configured skill nodes | 588 | | Character origins | 20 | | Custom Ponder lessons | 97 | | Authored construction definitions | 344 | | Startup scripts | 12 | | Server scripts | 76 | | Client scripts | 5 | The production definitions, skill tree and custom Ponder collection match the previously documented route. The beta also includes the quest-icon registration script and its artwork. ## Questbook progress The archive contains **42 chapter files and 1,036 quest records**. This includes the new layout, unfinished pages and inherited legacy chapters. It is not a count of finished quests for the rebuilt campaign. The new production chapters I–VII contain **143 records**. Chapters VIII–X have their pages in place but no quest records yet. The ten-chapter recipe progression exists independently of those unfinished quest pages. Town Square, Forging Ahead, Crafts & Curiosities, Realms & Relics and Seasonal Tales are the new group layout. The export also retains older groups and chapters, including references to removed mods. Those labels do not add mods to the Beta 1.0 inventory. ## Comparing with TK2 The baseline remains the actual **TK2 3.05 client archive**. Its manifest has 323 projects.
